questions.q: What is the core purpose of Tableau Desktop in this comparison?
options: It's the local authoring application where you connect to data and build workbooks — not a publishing destination itself
It's a free public-hosting website for finished dashboards
It's Tableau's paid, multi-tenant cloud product
It's a permissions and security add-on for Tableau Server
questions.explain: Tableau Desktop is the installed authoring application where the building happens. Public, Cloud, and Server are the three destinations you publish that work to.

questions.q: What is the key tradeoff of Tableau Public?
options: It's free, but everything published to it — the workbook and its underlying data — is visible to anyone on the internet
It's free, but limited to only bar charts and line charts
It costs the same as Tableau Cloud but has fewer chart types
It requires your own company's servers to run
questions.explain: Tableau Public trades privacy for cost — there's no private mode, which makes it wrong for company data but right for a public portfolio, like this course's Chapter 17 projects.

questions.q: What is the one structural difference between Tableau Cloud and Tableau Server?
options: They're the same product feature-for-feature; Cloud is hosted by Tableau in a multi-tenant SaaS environment, while Server is self-hosted by your own organization
Tableau Server has more chart types than Tableau Cloud
Tableau Cloud can't use permissions, subscriptions, or alerts
Tableau Server is free and Tableau Cloud is paid
questions.explain: Cloud and Server share the same underlying product and features — publishing, permissions, refreshes, subscriptions, alerts all work the same way. The difference is entirely about who hosts and manages the infrastructure.

questions.q: A healthcare company has strict rules about where patient data can physically reside. Which product best fits that requirement, and why?
options: Tableau Server, because the organization's own infrastructure hosts it, giving full control over data residency
Tableau Public, because it's free
Tableau Desktop alone, because nothing ever gets published
Tableau Cloud, because Tableau manages upgrades automatically
questions.explain: Tableau Server lets an organization control exactly where the server (and therefore the data) lives — on-premises or in cloud infrastructure the company itself manages — which is why compliance-heavy organizations often choose it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use original comparison diagrams instead of a real Tableau screenshot?
options: Because no single help.tableau.com page shows all four products side by side — this is an architectural/licensing comparison, not a single UI to photograph
Because Tableau doesn't allow its documentation images to be used
Because none of these four products actually have a user interface
Because this course never uses real screenshots
questions.explain: This is a conceptual comparison across four separate products rather than one interface, so after a genuine documentation search came up empty, the lesson uses original LTV-authored comparison diagrams instead of a claimed screenshot — the same honest approach used in Lesson 1.
